# Generational Wealth

> Generational Wealth is a disciplined swing & scalp trading community — a private Discord room where members get real-time trade callouts with defined entries, targets and invalidation, daily market commentary, and a risk-first system built to keep traders in the game. Membership is $120/month, billed via Patreon, cancel anytime.

Site: https://gwhlds.com
Operated by: Generational Wealth Holdings Corp.

**Important:** Generational Wealth is an educational trading community. It is NOT a registered broker-dealer, investment adviser, or signal-selling service, and it does not manage money or guarantee returns. All content is educational only.

## What Generational Wealth actually is

- A **private Discord community** for day, swing and scalp traders across forex, futures and equities.
- Every callout ships with a **clear entry level, defined upside targets, and a written invalidation point** — so the risk-to-reward is on the table before you enter.
- The room runs one **risk-first system**: position size comes from a fixed risk rule, not conviction. Losses stay small; winners are allowed to run.
- Members range from complete beginners to full-time traders. The education is the product as much as the callouts are.

## The Method — the three principles under every trade

1. **Break & hold.** We never chase. Price has to break clean through the called level *and hold* as the candle closes before anyone enters. Confirmation first, every single time.
2. **Know your next.** Every callout ships with a clear entry level, defined upside targets, and the next level price aims for — a plan before you click buy.
3. **Trail & protect.** As targets print one by one, the stop trails behind them to protect the gain. Profit that is given back was never profit.

## Membership

- **Price:** $120 per month, billed through Patreon.

- **Cancel:** anytime, directly through Patreon.
- **Includes:** private Discord access, real-time callouts with levels, daily commentary and breakdowns, and the risk-first education system.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is Generational Wealth?**
A private, membership-based swing and scalp trading community on Discord. Members receive real-time trade callouts with defined entries, targets and invalidation levels, plus daily market commentary and education built around a risk-first system.

**How much does it cost?**
$120 per month, billed via Patreon. There is no long-term contract and members can cancel at any time.

**Is this financial advice?**
No. Generational Wealth Holdings Corp. is not a registered broker-dealer or investment adviser. Everything published is educational only and is not a recommendation to buy, sell or hold any instrument. Trading carries substantial risk of loss.

**Do I need experience to join?**
No. The room is built for beginners through advanced traders. New members are taught the same risk-first process the experienced members run, starting with position sizing and invalidation.

**What markets does the room trade?**
Primarily forex and futures, with equities setups as they appear. The method — break and hold, defined targets, trailing protection — is applied the same way across all of them.

**Is it day trading or swing trading?**
Both. It is a swing *and* scalp room. Some setups are intraday scalps; others are held for days. Both are sized from the same risk rule.

**Are results guaranteed?**
No. No trading community can guarantee results, and Generational Wealth does not. Every trade a member takes is their own decision and their own risk.

- [What Is Leverage in Trading?](https://gwhlds.com/hub/what-is-leverage-in-trading.html): how the leverage ratio and the margin percentage are one number, the published caps for US retail forex and EU retail CFDs, the drawdown math that decides how much is too much, and why effective leverage should fall out of your stop distance.
- [What Is a Margin Call and How to Never Get One](https://gwhlds.com/hub/what-is-a-margin-call.html): Regulation T's 50% initial and FINRA's 25% maintenance requirement, the exact price that triggers a call, why a firm can liquidate without notice, how futures and forex differ, and the six habits that prevent one.
- [10 Mistakes That Blow Up New Trading Accounts](https://gwhlds.com/hub/mistakes-that-blow-up-trading-accounts.html): sizing from conviction, no written invalidation, moving stops, averaging down, overtrading, revenge trading, chasing entries, no daily loss limit, ignoring round-trip cost, and abandoning a system mid-drawdown — with the fix for each.
- [How to Build a Trading Plan You'll Actually Follow](https://gwhlds.com/hub/how-to-build-a-trading-plan.html): the eight sections a plan needs, how to convert vague intentions into executable if-then rules, the research on implementation intentions, and how to test a plan before trusting it with size.
- [What Is a Trading Journal?](https://gwhlds.com/hub/trading-journal.html): the twelve fields worth logging, why rule compliance matters more than profit, the metrics that mean something versus the ones that mislead, and the disposition effect a journal is built to catch.
- [Risk Management in Trading](https://gwhlds.com/hub/risk-management-trading.html): risk management as a system of five layers — risk per trade, written invalidation, position sizing, daily and weekly loss caps, and a drawdown rule — with what each layer catches and why the order matters.
- [The 1% Rule in Trading](https://gwhlds.com/hub/the-1-percent-rule-in-trading.html): what the 1% actually caps and what it does not, the survival table across losing streaks, why an optimal stake is a fraction of capital rather than a fixed sum, and when 1% is the wrong number.
- [How to Set a Stop Loss That Isn't Just a Guess](https://gwhlds.com/hub/how-to-set-a-stop-loss.html): the four placement methods compared — structure, volatility, fixed percentage and time — why wide stops are not risky once sized correctly, what a stop order does not guarantee, and the four places a stop should never sit.
- [What Is Invalidation in Trading?](https://gwhlds.com/hub/what-is-invalidation-in-trading.html): the difference between an invalidation and the stop that executes it, the three forms invalidation takes, how to write one a stranger could apply, and why sunk cost makes traders hold past it.
- [Why Most New Traders Quit in the First Year](https://gwhlds.com/hub/why-new-traders-quit.html): the day trader survival data, the five reasons an account runs out of runway before the skill arrives, and the specific changes that keep people trading.
- [How to Size a Position From Risk, Not Conviction](https://gwhlds.com/hub/position-sizing-from-risk.html): the position sizing formula worked through for stocks, forex and futures, why conviction sizing puts the most money on the worst trades, and what to do when the answer is below one tradeable unit.
- [What Is a Trailing Stop, and When to Actually Use One](https://gwhlds.com/hub/what-is-a-trailing-stop.html): how a trailing stop differs from a fixed stop, the three ways to trail, why a triggered trailing stop guarantees no execution price, and the two habits that turn winning trades into scratches.
- [How to Take Partial Profits Without Capping Your Winners](https://gwhlds.com/hub/how-to-take-partial-profits.html): what a partial costs on a big winner priced in R, three scale-out plans compared, the disposition-effect evidence behind the urge to close early, and how partials and trailing stops fit together.
- [Drawdown Explained: How Much Is Normal?](https://gwhlds.com/hub/drawdown-explained.html): the recovery arithmetic from 5% to 90%, the difference between peak-to-valley and maximum drawdown, what regulators require professionals to disclose, and how to write a three-tier stopping rule.
- [Risk of Ruin: The Math Nobody Shows New Traders](https://gwhlds.com/hub/risk-of-ruin.html): the gambler's ruin table across win rates and bet sizes, why position size matters far more than win rate, what the model gets wrong, and why no edge means ruin is only a matter of time.
